note: Startup stall fix (Issue #71): verifyPermission in vault.ts races queryPermission against a 15000ms timeout (same value as the existing EXCLUSIVE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS fail-safe); on timeout it returns false (permission unconfirmed, never granted), so restoreVaultHandle settles into the designed needs-permission state instead of hanging forever. The ChatScreen startup chain gains a rejection handler on the startup-lock promise that settles vaultStatus instead of leaving it at checking forever. Round 2 (Codex P2 on PR #72): the rejection handler settles to the dedicated startup-failed state (recovery by page reload only, offered by a banner mirroring the unsupported-journal-version one) instead of not-connected, because with tabVaultEpoch unset (fail-closed) the normal reconnect commit guard and withVaultWorldRead reject everything, so the reconnect flow could never recover; the VaultStatus type gains the startup-failed member with its rationale comment. Exact added / removed lines of vault.ts and ChatScreen.tsx only (never a pattern).
